notes: Each case is a claim an agent might make, paired with the quote it would pass to the cite tool to support it. `expect: verified` means findQuote must anchor the quote in the live document; `expect: rejected` means it must not — the cite tool and the legal plugin's verification ladder must refuse it and the agent must never present it. Anchoring is exact except that any whitespace run matches any other (mammoth/pdf extraction normalizes whitespace); everything else — wording, punctuation, case, numbers, ellipses — must match the document byte for byte. run.ts executes these cases offline against the real findQuote from lib/extract.ts.

cases.claim: Breach exposes the discloser to harm that damages cannot remedy, supporting injunctive relief.
cases.quote: irreparable harm for which monetary damages would be an inadequate remedy

cases.claim: Same passage copied across a line break — whitespace runs are normalized by design, so this still anchors.
cases.quote: irreparable harm for which monetary  damages would be an inadequate remedy

cases.claim: The agreement is governed by Delaware law.
cases.quote: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of Delaware
cases.why: The document says 'is governed by and construed in accordance with' — a close paraphrase that swaps in the more common 'shall be governed by' phrasing must still be rejected.

cases.claim: Confidential Information must be returned or deleted on termination.
cases.quote: return or delete all Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party
cases.why: The document says 'return or destroy'. One substituted word in an otherwise verbatim quote must be rejected.

cases.claim: The receiving party must return or destroy Confidential Information.
cases.quote: The Receiving Party shall ... return or destroy all Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party
cases.why: Both fragments are real but the ellipsis is not in the document. The cite tool forbids added ellipses; a spliced quote must be rejected, not silently stitched.

cases.claim: The receiving party indemnifies the discloser for breaches.
cases.quote: the Receiving Party shall indemnify the Disclosing Party against all losses arising from any breach of this Agreement
cases.why: There is no indemnity in this NDA at all. Plausible boilerplate that appears nowhere in the document is the core hallucination case.

cases.claim: Confidentiality obligations survive for three years.
cases.quote: for a period of three (3) years from the date of disclosure
cases.why: The document says five (5) years. A quote with an altered number misstates the deal term and must be rejected.

cases.claim: Either party may terminate on thirty days' notice.
cases.quote: thirty (30) days prior written notice to the other Party
cases.why: The document reads "thirty (30) days' prior written notice" — the dropped apostrophe makes the quote non-verbatim. Only whitespace differences are tolerated.

cases.claim: The agreement bars soliciting the other party's employees.
cases.quote: neither Party will solicit for employment any employee of the other Party
cases.why: Standard NDA language, but this NDA has no non-solicitation clause. Quoting market boilerplate the document does not contain must be rejected.

cases.claim: Confidential Information is provided as-is, without warranty.
cases.quote: All Confidential Information is provided "as is."
cases.why: The document renders this clause in capitals: ALL CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION IS PROVIDED "AS IS." Matching is case-sensitive; a re-cased quote is not the document's text.
